Copper-Catalyzed Phosphorylation of 2,3-Allenoic Acids and
Phosphine Oxide: Access to Phosphorylated Butenolides
Tianshuo Zhong, Xiangyun Zheng, Chuanliu Yin, Qitao Shen, and Chuanming Yu *
Cite This: J. Org. Chem. 2021, 86, 9699 −9710 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: We investigated a novel Cu-catalyzed annulation of 2,3-allenoic acids with diphenylphosphine oxide, leading to the
formation of 4-phosphate butenolides in up to 88% yield. The formation of the C −P bond provides new avenues for the
functionalization of diﬀerent furan-2(5H)-ones, with favorable features such as suitable functional group tolerance and mild synthesis
conditions.
■ INTRODUCTION
As e ﬀective sca ﬀolds, furan-2(5 H)-ones are widespread in
natural products, bioactive molecules, and drugs ( Figure 1 ).1
Therefore, developing a valid and e ﬃcient method for their
synthesis represents a key goal in organic synthesis. 2 For
instance, Ma et al. originally developed a method for the
cyclization of halogenated metals and allenoic acids to a ﬀord β-
halobutenolides ( Scheme 1 a).3 Subsequent studies have
achieved C −C bond formation of allenoic acids with aryl
iodides,4 alkenes,5 alkynes,6 or allenes7 to form polysubstituted
butenolides ( Scheme 1 b). Afterward, various C −S bond
formation reactions, including tri ﬂuoromethylthiolation, sulfe-
nylation, sulfonylation, and selenylation have been widely
reported ( Scheme 1 c).8 Despite these remarkable advances,
the exploration of other functional groups to prepare di ﬀerent
types of functionalized butenolides remains a critical task.
Phosphorus-containing heterocycles are an important class
of organophosphorus compounds, applied widely in synthetic 9
and medicinal chemistry, 10 as well as material science 11 and
universal ligands, 12 drawing considerable attention for both
industrial and medicinal applications. Generally, the traditional
synthesis of phosphorus-substituted heterocycles is based on
direct phosphorylation of the parent heterocycles.
13 Various
eﬀective C −P bond reactions involving the addition of P-
centered radicals to initiate the formation of the heterocycle
have recently been developed. 14 It is worth noting that this
kind of reaction is e ﬃcient and functional as the phosphorus-
substituted heterocycle is formed with the concomitant
combination of a phosphorus portion. However, only few
methods for the introduction of phosphorus substituents into
furan-2(5H)-ones have been reported. Therefore, the identi-
ﬁcation of a method for preparing phosphorus-containing
furanones is a highly valuable task. Based on our previous
investigation of radical synthesis,
15 in this study, we report the
preparation of a phosphorus-containing furanone via the highly
eﬃcient Cu-catalyzed annulati on of allenoic acids with
phosphorus, which directly forms C −P bonds and creates
furanone rings in one reaction. ( Scheme 1 d).
■ RESULTS AND DISCUSSION
As shown in Table 1, the radical phosphorylation of 2-methyl-
4-phenyl-2,3-allenoic acid ( 1a) was chosen as a model
reaction, with diphenylphosphine oxide ( 2a) as the phospho-
rus source. The reaction was carried out in the presence of
FeCl

CH3CN/HOAc solution, providing the desired product in 17%
yield. Among the various screened catalysts (entries 1−7),
Cu(OAc)2 was proved to be the most suitable one, giving the
product in 80% yield (entry 5). Other oxidants such as TBHP,

(entries 8−10). Based on these results, it was critical for the
success of the reaction to use an acid as the cosolvent (entry
11). On the other hand, using formic acid instead of HOAc or
adjusting the CH
3CN/HOAc ratio did not improve the
eﬃciency of the reaction (entries 12−14). Lastly, further
decrease in 2a concentration and reaction temperature resulted
in lower yields (entries 15, 16 ). Therefore, the optimal
reaction conditions were as follows: 1a (0.2 mmol), 2a (0.4
mmol), K 2S2O8 (0.4 mmol), Cu(OAc) 2 (20 mol %), and
CH3CN/HOAc = 3:1 (2 mL).
We investigated the range of allenes substrates after
determining the optimal reaction conditions ( Scheme 2 ).
Benzene rings bearing electron-donating groups, such as -CH 3,
t-C(CH3)3, and -OCH 3, at the para position reacted with the
diphenylphosphine oxide 2a to deliver the phosphated
butenolides 3b−3d in 42 −70% yields. On the other hand,
functional groups such as ﬂuoro, chloro, bromo, and
triﬂuoromethyl in the para position of the aryl ring were well
tolerated, and the products 3e−3h were acquired in 48 −82%
yields. Substrates present in the meta ( 3i) and ortho (3j−3l)
positions of the aryl groups reacted smoothly, providing the
corresponding products in 37 −77% yields. The desired
products 3m and 3n were provided in high yields both
electron-deﬁcient (CF
3) groups and electron-donating (Me)
on the phenyl ring. In addition, the substrate with naphthyl as
the R
1 substituent could also react with diphenylphosphine
oxide (2a)t oa ﬀord the corresponding product 3o in moderate
yield (51%); the slight decrease in yield might be due to steric
hindrance e ﬀects. It is rather remarkable that this type of
reaction could also be utilized for the substrate with n-propyl
as the R
3 substituent (3p). Similarly, both Ph and Me groups at
the R2 position led to lower yields ( 3q and 3r) because of
steric hindrance. 14i
To further expand the versatility of the phosphorylated
reaction, we next explored the range of 2 using the optimized
reaction conditions shown in Scheme 3 . First, di ﬀerent
aromatic substituents ( −CH3, −OMe, −F, −Cl, −Br, and
−Ph) were found to be compatible with the optimized
conditions, giving the ﬁnal products 4a−4g in moderate to
excellent yields (58 −88%). However, the disubstituted
substrate 4h was found to be less tolerated in the present
reaction, giving 43% yield. The reaction was further extended
to other H-phosphonate, disopropyl, and diethyl phosphites
that reacted well with allenoic acids ( 1a), generating the
corresponding products 4i−4j in 31−33% yields. Interestingly,
the reaction of the asymmetric H-phosphinate ester proceeded
smoothly, providing product 4k in 41% yield.
In order to investigate the potential applications of the
present approach, a gram-scale experiment was carried out,
providing the corresponding product 3a in 62% yield ( Scheme
4). Moreover, the ring-opening reaction of 3a with t-BuOH
delivered the 1,4-dicarbonyl compound in 42% yield, which is
an important precursor and intermediate in organic syn-
thesis.
16
A series of control experiments were conducted to better
understand the phosphorylation mechanism ( Scheme 5 ).
Although the reaction was completely suppressed when the
radical trapping reagents (2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidin-1-yl)-
oxyl (TEMPO) and butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) were

conditions, a BHT -2a adduct was detected by high-resolution

might be involved in the process ( Scheme 5 a,b). In the
absence of K
2S2O8, no phosphorylated product was delivered,
which proved the important role of the oxidant in radical
cyclization reaction ( Scheme 5 c). In addition, this reaction
could occur without the copper catalyst, giving product 3a in a
limited yield ( Scheme 5d). On the other hand, the reaction of
AlCl
3 and ZnCl2, instead of Cu(OAc) 2, as Lewis acids did not
yield the desired product 3a. These results indicated that
Cu(OAc)2 may not play the role of a Lewis acid ( Scheme 5e).
Finally, when 6 reacted with the H −P(O) compound 2a under
standard conditions, product 3a was not formed. These results
clearly indicate that 2,3-allenoic acids may not ﬁrst undergo
intramolecular cyclization to form 6 and then react with the
phosphoryl radical ( Scheme 5 f).
Based on the control experiments discussed above and
previous studies, we believe that the present reaction may
proceed through the free radical pathway illustrated in Scheme
6. First, in the presence of K
2S2O8, diphenylphosphine oxide
undergoes a deprotonation process to generate a P-centered
radical (Path A). In path B, Cu(II) oxidizes the tautomer of
diphenylphosphine oxide and deprotonates to generate the
radical, while K
2S2O8 oxidizes Cu(I) to obtain Cu(II). 17
Subsequently, the phosphoryl radical attacks 2,3-allylic acid
(1a) to obtain the free radical intermediate A. Next, the
oxidation of the free radical species generates the allyl cation B.
Lastly, the intermediate B provides the phosphorylated
product 3 through the process of intramolecular nucleophilic
attack.
■ CONCLUSIONS
In summary, a Cu-catalyzed phosphorylation of 2,3-allenoic
acids has been explored, providing a series of 4-phosphate
butenolides in up to 88% yield. The meaningful features of this
approach include mild reaction conditions, inexpensive metal
catalysts, broad substrate applicability, and high functional
group tolerance. Importantly, all the obtained phosphated
butenolides have not been previously synthesized and might
ﬁnd potential applications in medicinal chemistry. Therefore,
this method provides a superior alternative to the formation of
Cs p
2−p bonds for the direct synthesis of furan-2(5 H)-ones.
